channel.title: Can AI outgrow the planet’s power grid?
channel.description: An interactive series by Akarsh Gopal on AI and electricity: what AI uses now, what the money will build, and whether the grid can connect it.

item.title: Can AI outgrow the planet’s power grid?
item.description: Contents and map of an interactive series on AI and electricity: what AI uses now, what the money will build, whether the grid can connect it this decade, and the long-run case.

item.title: From Switch to Supercluster: Can the Grid Keep Up?
item.description: The series in one essay: how switches became computers, computers became cheap enough to learn from data, learning became a gigawatt-scale industry, and whether the grid can connect what AI is buying this decade.

item.title: The Yardstick: How Big Is the Bar?
item.description: Where AI inference sits among the world’s energy sinks, and the three bars it would have to beat: 10% of electricity, the largest electricity end-use, and the largest end-use of all energy.

item.title: Rules: Switch, Gate, Adder, Program
item.description: An interactive explainer: two switches that add, a relay that throws a relay, and a machine that can imitate any other. What a computation is, physically.

item.title: The Price of a Flip
item.description: An interactive explainer: how cheaply a bit can flip, from vacuum tubes to 2 nm transistors, why Dennard scaling ended, and what that means for the energy AI can spend.

item.title: Parallel: Why GPUs Won
item.description: An interactive explainer: neural networks are almost all multiply-adds, and the hardware that wins is the one that moves the fewest bytes per multiply. Matrices, the roofline, systolic arrays, thousands of threads, fewer bits and the cost of distance.

item.title: A Model Is a Function You Can Tune
item.description: An interactive explainer: a neuron is a line, two layers draw XOR, backpropagation passes the blame, and gradient descent rolls downhill. What a model is, before tokens and transformers.

item.title: Language: Tokens to Next Word
item.description: An interactive explainer: convolutions, sequence memory, attention, and predicting the next word. What one answer costs in operations.

item.title: Scaling: The Bet That Loss Is Predictable
item.description: An interactive explainer: language-model loss falls along a straight line on a log plot of compute, which turned AI into a capital, data and energy project. Scaling laws, compute-optimal training, the frontier, the data wall, the data flywheel and the bill.

item.title: The Data: Scale of the Collection
item.description: How much text, how many people, how much time and money went into AI training data — and where it goes. The examples branch of the case.

item.title: The Demand: Who Asks, How Often?
item.description: Counting the tokens Google, OpenAI and Microsoft publish, turning them into electricity and reconciling them with a top-down estimate; then what 2026 capital spending buys in gigawatts.

item.title: The AI Factory: Chips, Cooling and the Grid
item.description: An interactive explainer: where the power of an AI data centre goes, from one 700 W chip to a 150 MW campus, how the heat is carried away, why the servers never sleep, and what that asks of the grid.

item.title: What Binds, 2026–30: Chips, Power, Permits or Money?
item.description: What limits AI’s growth this decade: firm power, grid connections and transformers, chips and memory, permits, or money. A ranking with the evidence, mostly from the United States.

item.title: Orbital Compute: Is Space the Only Answer?
item.description: Sunlight, radiators, mass per kilowatt and launch price: when orbital data centres beat the grid, and when they do not. Star-mind as a coda.

item.title: The Verdict: What the Ledger Says
item.description: Scenario ledger for Act 1 and Act 2: Low, Mid and High paths, the three rungs, 100× by 2035, and what would flip the answer.
